text:
Barclay Goodrow has two Stanley Cup rings from Tampa Bay and an "A" on his sweater in San Jose, where his career began as an undrafted free agent. At 33, his role is the one he has always played: bottom-six minutes (11.5 a night), the penalty kill, and plenty of contact, 41 hits in 19 games.

It hasn't been a good stretch. The Sharks have lost five straight, and after the loss in Dallas on Nov. 7 Goodrow was blunt about the penalty kill. In Yahoo Sports' headline: "Not Getting the Job Done." At five on five the numbers are no kinder. San Jose has had 36% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and the team has actually scored more than those chances deserve in his minutes, so there's no bad luck to point to.

On his own shots he has been a little unlucky: no goals on 1.74 expected, a small miss over 19 games rather than a crisis. We'd watch the penalty kill more than his point total (our projection says about six goals the rest of the way), because killing penalties is the job he's there to do.
headline: Barclay Goodrow and a penalty kill under pressure
